title.narrative: SPVO – Improving the living incomes and future of coffee farming families in Sidama, through specialty coffee

description.narrative: Ethiopia is Africa's largest coffee producer. Still, there is a lot to gain in terms of quality, quantity, and social sustainability conditions of employees and producers. Especially, Ethiopia has one of the highest child labour rates in the world, with children often employed at coffee farms and mills. In turn, working conditions at especially mills are deplorable. Finally, people often do not earn living wages, have an uncertain income, and do not know how to manage their incomes. Low wages are a likely main trigger for the other social issues, which are therefore likely to occur continuously.Bette Buna B.V. (specialty importer of Ethiopian (green) Arabica coffee), DDM Trading PLC (a producing and exporting specialty coffee company in Ethiopia), and Joni (an Ethiopian based non-governmental organisation (NGO) on farmer capacity building, multi stakeholder alignment, and community development), have jointly formed a project partnership with the motivation to improve social sustainability in the coffee value chain in Ethiopia.The main reason to engage in social sustainability improvement for the partners is their social-impact related nature. Improving social sustainability aligns with their commitment to human rights, fair labour practices, and community development. In turn, the partnership can contribute to creating a stable, reliable supply chain less prone to disruptions by addressing social sustainability. This stability ensures a consistent supply of high-quality coffee beans.Moreover, compliance with the European Union Regulation on Deforestation-free Products (EUDR) and corporate sustainable due diligence (CSDDD) regulation, assuring the farmers can sustain their activities, is important to the project partners.A final reason is that the project partners want to meet the changing consumer demands for higher quality and experience based, sustainable coffee. Nowadays, consumers are more concerned about the social impact of the coffee they purchase. By committing to social sustainability in the Ethiopian coffee supply chain, the project partners meet the growing demand for sustainably produced coffee, enhancing their brand's reputation and fostering customer loyalty.
